title: Your Own Unit Test Framework
description:
```cpp
TEST(fractions_add) { CHECK(1 + 1 == 2); }
TEST(strings) { CHECK_EQ(std::string{ "ab" } + "c", "abc"); }
```
```
[ok]   fractions_add
[FAIL] strings  main.cpp:12  expected "abc", got "abd"
2 tests, 1 failed
```
hints: Registration: the macro declares a function, then a static object whose constructor adds that function and its name to a global `std::vector`. Statics are built before `main` (lesson 13.06).

`CHECK` must know which test is running so it can mark it failed: keep a global "current test" pointer that `runAll` sets before calling each test. `std::source_location::current()` as a default argument gives the file and line.
requirements: A `TEST(name)` macro that defines a test function and registers it automatically, before `main` runs
`CHECK(condition)` and `CHECK_EQ(a, b)` that record a failure with the file and line instead of stopping
A `runAll()` that runs every test, prints one line per test and a summary, and returns a non-zero exit code if anything failed
Filtering: run only the tests whose name contains a word given on the command line
stretch: `CHECK_THROWS_AS(expression, Type)`, timing each test, and coloured output.
